The aggregate revenue figures would require substantial primary research (3PL revenue filings, industry surveys). Single secondary-trade source. Low.

claims_detail.claim: Surge Transportation filed Chapter 11 in 2024, confirming Convoy's closure was not isolated
claims_detail.rationale: Same Brush Pass Research blog. A Chapter 11 filing is a court record (primary-legal) — that is the authoritative source. Only a secondary blog cited. Low. The fact itself is likely accurate and cross-verifiable via PACER, but not cited from there.

claims_detail.claim: Average freight brokerage net revenue margin ~15%; $1,912 revenue per load; minimum sustainable margin ~11.3%
claims_detail.rationale: Same Brush Pass Research blog. Operating cost/margin figures from a single small analyst blog. Trade-press-only override for margin figures. Low.

claims_detail.claim: $75,000 surety bond requirement for freight brokers has been unchanged since 1980; this covers fewer than 2 average-size fraud loads at $40,760/load
claims_detail.rationale: FreightWaves trade press (source 47). The $75K bond requirement is codified in 49 CFR 387.307 — a regulatory citation (primary-gov) exists but is not cited. The historical bond amount and date are verifiable from CFR, not from trade press. The calculation ($40,760/load = <2 loads covered) uses a TIA figure (single-source) as the comparator. Two weak sources combined. Low.

claims_detail.claim: Convoy raised ~$900M–$1B+ at a $3.8B valuation 18 months before its October 2023 closure
claims_detail.rationale: Multiple trade outlets (FreightWaves, TechCrunch, Trucking Dive, Axios — sources 7, 31, 50) reported the Convoy valuation and funding. Convoy's funding rounds were disclosed through SEC Form D filings. Multiple independent secondary sources with strong corroboration signal. Scores Medium: 3+ independent news/trade outlets all corroborating a factual closure event and funding history, though no Form D is directly cited.

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim: Industry-wide double brokering fraud losses $500M–$800M+ per year; per-load cost ~$40,760; per-company avg loss $402,344
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: All dollar loss figures trace to a single source: TIA 2024 fraud survey, propagated through multiple trade publications (truckingdive, freightcaviar) that all cite the same TIA report. Chain-of-citations = 1 source. No independent audit, government crime statistics, or insurance claims data cross-validates. The $40,760 per-load figure is the single most-cited cost anchor in Stage 2 across PP-2.1, PP-2.4, PP-2.5, and appears in VC4 — making it high downstream impact across the entire stage.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.specific_question_to_research: What does the FBI Internet Crime Report or NICB (National Insurance Crime Bureau) annual report say about freight fraud losses? Does the FMCSA's own complaint database or C-TPAT/CBP data provide independent aggregate estimates of freight fraud losses?
weak_claims_for_deep_research.evidence_type_needed: primary-gov (FBI IC3, NICB, FMCSA complaint data), primary-legal (consolidated insurance claim statistics from a major cargo insurer's annual report), or primary-association (TT Club or BIMCO cargo theft annual statistics)

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim: FMCSA: ~92% of ~780,000 registered US motor carriers are 'unrated'
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: The 92% unrated figure is foundational to RC2 in PP-2.1 and RC2 in PP-2.4 — repeated across both pain points as the structural root cause. The source is a GetTransport.com blog, not FMCSA directly. This is a chain-of-citations failure: the primary source (FMCSA SAFER Web carrier database) exists and is publicly accessible at safer.fmcsa.dot.gov but is not cited.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.specific_question_to_research: Pull the FMCSA SAFER carrier statistics page directly: how many active US motor carriers have a safety rating of Satisfactory, Conditional, Unsatisfactory, or Not Rated? The data is publicly available at safer.fmcsa.dot.gov/RegistrationItems/Stats.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.evidence_type_needed: primary-gov: FMCSA SAFER system carrier count by rating status (fmcsa.dot.gov/safety/carrier-safety/carrier-safety-statistics)

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim: Indonesia logistics cost is 24% of GDP
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: This is the foundational cost-of-inefficiency claim for the SEA/Indonesia TMS gap (PP-2.3) and is used to establish market need. Source is an East Ventures VC investor blog post about their portfolio company Waresix — a commercial document. This figure is frequently cited in Indonesia logistics reports but the primary source is never cited directly. If this traces to BPS Indonesia, World Bank, or an ADB study, citing the primary is essential for credibility.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.specific_question_to_research: What is the primary source for Indonesia logistics cost as % of GDP? Search World Bank Indonesia country reports, ADB Indonesia logistics assessments, and BPS Indonesia GDP expenditure data for 2022–2024.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.evidence_type_needed: primary-multilateral (World Bank Indonesia logistics study or ADB logistics cost assessment), primary-gov (BPS Indonesia, Kemenhub transport statistics), or primary-consultancy (McKinsey/BCG report on Indonesia logistics authored with named country)

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim: Approximately 70% of FTL contracts go unused, with shippers redirecting lanes to spot
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: This is an extraordinary and counterintuitive claim: that nearly three-quarters of contracted freight is not used under the contracted terms. Source is Amazon Freight's newsroom — Amazon Freight is itself a freight brokerage competitor with direct commercial incentive to highlight the failure of traditional contracted freight to sell its own spot/managed services. Press-release-only override. No independent logistics research firm, academic paper, or government transportation agency cited.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.specific_question_to_research: Does MIT Center for Transportation and Logistics, CSCMP (Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals), or any peer-reviewed logistics journal document FTL contract utilization rates? Search for 'routing guide compliance rate FTL contracts' in CSCMP publications and Journal of Business Logistics.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.evidence_type_needed: primary-association (CSCMP State of Logistics Report), primary-academic (peer-reviewed supply chain journal), or primary-consultancy (McKinsey/BCG study on freight procurement effectiveness)

weak_claims_for_deep_research.claim: Freight brokerage gross revenue declined 15.1% in 2023 from $159B to $135B
weak_claims_for_deep_research.why_weak: Macro brokerage revenue aggregate used to establish the scale of PP-2.5 (broker solvency risk). Source is a single small analyst blog (Brush Pass Research) with unknown methodology. No TIA industry report, FMCSA revenue data, public 3PL earnings aggregation, or CSCMP State of Logistics Report is cited. The $159B→$135B figure is highly specific yet unverifiable from the cited source.
weak_claims_for_deep_research.specific_question_to_research: What does the CSCMP 2024 State of Logistics Report state about US freight brokerage industry revenue in 2023? Does Armstrong & Associates (a recognized 3PL research firm) or SJ Consulting Group publish independent US freight brokerage market size estimates?
weak_claims_for_deep_research.evidence_type_needed: primary-association (CSCMP State of Logistics 2024, Armstrong & Associates 3PL market study), primary-consultancy (Armstrong & Associates, Gartner Logistics Research if attributed), or primary-filing (public broker earnings aggregations from C.H. Robinson, XPO, Echo Global 10-K filings)

remediation_needed: Pain point count (5) exceeds IMI target of 2-4. PP-2.3 (SMB TMS gap) and PP-2.5 (broker solvency risk) were flagged by the researcher as new pain points not in the original hypothesis — these should be reviewed by the orchestrator to decide whether to fold, drop, or promote to full status before final compilation.

PP-2.2 citation count: sources (15)-(19) total 5 base sources for the pain point, of which 4 are from the same domain (gosonar.com). Single-domain override applies — effective unique source count for PP-2.2 core claims is ~2, well below IMI floor of 8. Deep research required to widen source diversity.
PP-2.5 citation count: core economic claims (PP-2.5-2, PP-2.5-4) rest on a single Brush Pass Research blog. Effective unique source count for broker economics claims is 1. Below IMI floor.

Source diversity: of 52 unique sources, only 5 qualify as primary-tier (VC20, VC24, VC26, VC30, PP-2.2-9/PP-2.4-4, PP-2.3-5). All five are in different primary sub-categories. 9.6% primary-tier source rate is low for a research corpus.

APAC/SEA market sizing: all market-size figures for the SEA/ASEAN context are Low confidence (aggregator sources only). No government statistics body or multilateral agency data cited for TMS/freight-procurement software market size at country level — as acknowledged in the data-gap section. This remains an unresolved structural gap.

gate_reasoning: Stage 2 carries 66.1% Low-confidence claims and 10.7% Speculative — a combined weak-source rate of 76.8%. Only 5 of 56 claims (8.9%) are High, all grounded in SEC filings or Federal Register documents. The structural problems are systemic rather than incidental: the dominant cost figures for PP-2.1 (fraud losses) all trace to a single TIA member survey; all PP-2.2 quantitative claims trace to FreightWaves SONAR (single commercial data product domain); PP-2.5 broker economics rest on a single small analyst blog. The foundational Indonesia logistics cost claim (24% of GDP) is sourced only from a VC investor blog. Nine vendor self-citations triggered the vendor-marketing override. The pain point count (5) exceeds the IMI 2-4 target, and two pain points (PP-2.3, PP-2.5) were flagged by the researcher as outside the original working hypotheses — these need orchestrator review before deep research resources are allocated. Deep research should prioritize: (1) FMCSA.gov direct carrier rating statistics to replace the chain-of-citations 92% unrated claim, (2) FBI IC3 or NICB data to cross-validate the $40,760 per-load fraud cost anchor, (3) World Bank or ADB primary source for Indonesia 24% GDP logistics cost, (4) CSCMP or Armstrong & Associates for the 15.1% brokerage revenue decline figure, and (5) direct SCOTUS record for Montgomery v. Caribe ruling. Ship-as-is would propagate five load-bearing Low-confidence figures into the final corpus without cross-validation.
